hints: Focus on the conditions for each reaction, especially whether the mixture is acidic or alkaline at the end.
Remember that hydrolysing a nitrile in acid gives the free carboxylic acid, while hydrolysing it in alkali gives its salt instead.
Check the oxidation reactions too, strong oxidation under reflux of ethanol and ethanal both stops at the carboxylic acid stage.
walkthrough:
**Recall the two routes to ethanoic acid**

There are two families here. Nitriles can be hydrolysed to acids, and primary alcohols and aldehydes can be oxidised to acids. The key is the exact conditions.

General ideas:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CHO} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$

**Compare acid vs alkaline hydrolysis of ethanenitrile**

With dilute acid, you get the free acid plus an ammonium ion. With dilute alkali, you get the carboxylate salt plus ammonia, not the free acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + \text{H}^{+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^{+}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + \text{OH}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-} + \text{NH}_3$$

**Check the oxidation reactions under reflux**

Acidified dichromate(VI) is a strong oxidising agent. Under reflux, ethanal is oxidised once, and ethanol is oxidised twice, both ending at ethanoic acid.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + [\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + 2[\text{O}] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Pick the one that does not give the free acid**

Options B, C and D all finish as $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$. Only heating with dilute sodium hydroxide finishes as sodium ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-}\text{Na}^{+}$, so no free ethanoic acid is obtained directly.

options.A: Correct. Alkaline hydrolysis of ethanenitrile gives the ethanoate ion, not ethanoic acid: $\text{CH}_3\text{CN} + \text{OH}^{-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO}^{-} + \text{NH}_3$. You would need a separate acidification step to get $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.
options.B: Incorrect. Acid hydrolysis of a nitrile does give the free carboxylic acid. Here $\text{CH}_3\text{CN}$ with dilute $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ gives $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{NH}_4^{+}$.
options.C: Incorrect. Ethanal is an aldehyde and is easily oxidised by acidified dichromate(VI) under reflux to ethanoic acid in one step.
options.D: Incorrect. Ethanol is a primary alcohol. With excess strong oxidant and heating under reflux, it is oxidised via ethanal all the way to ethanoic acid.
